# Azure Private DNS Resolver — facts

> Source-anchored units about Azure Private DNS Resolver: 17 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · 17 units · 6 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] Inbound endpoint addresses support static or dynamic allocation. A dynamic address stays unchanged during normal operation but can change when the endpoint is reprovisioned, so forwarder configuration must account for that lifecycle. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Create only the endpoints required by query direction: inbound for external clients querying Azure-visible names; outbound plus forwarding rules for Azure queries sent to external DNS servers. Bidirectional deployments can need both. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Each resolver endpoint needs a separate, dedicated subnet delegated to Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers. Microsoft documents supported endpoint subnet sizes from /28 through /24; the subnet cannot host another service. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-22) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] An outbound endpoint uses a dedicated subnet but has no provisioned listener IP like an inbound endpoint; configure forwarding rulesets rather than pointing clients at an outbound endpoint IP. (low confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver
- [statement] Microsoft rejects 168.63.129.16 as a forwarding-rule destination with the error "Exception while making add request for rule". Use an appropriate reachable DNS server target rather than that Azure platform address. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/
- [statement] Chris Hailes provides an original Bicep deployment example containing resolver, inbound endpoint, outbound endpoint, forwarding ruleset, VNet link and forwarding-rule resources; the example illustrates the resource dependencies, rather than proving production readiness. (low confidence) — https://blog.brewedinthecloud.com/p/azure-dns-privateresolver/ · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Azure DNS Private Resolver provides managed recursive resolution and conditional forwarding between Azure and external networks; inbound endpoints receive queries, while outbound endpoints apply forwarding rulesets. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets
- [statement] An on-premises conditional forwarder targets the inbound endpoint's private IP over existing private connectivity. That endpoint resolves private zones linked to its own VNet. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets
- [statement] Azure clients using Azure-provided DNS consult linked private zones before forwarding rulesets. Matching forwarding rules use the most specific DNS suffix; unmatched queries proceed through Azure DNS. Custom VNet DNS settings send queries to the configured custom servers instead. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets
- [statement] A ruleset that forwards a namespace to an inbound endpoint must not be linked to that endpoint's own VNet: the configuration can create a DNS forwarding loop. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://naxaya.com/articles/azure-dns-private-resolver-diagnose-forwarding-loop-before-changing-zones/
- [statement] For Atlas, resolver deployment is conditional on DNS requirements, not an established universal prerequisite. This is a synthesis: Azure documents hybrid forwarding, while Atlas documents endpoint-specific connection strings resolving to private interface IPs. DNS success alone does not establish database connectivity. (medium confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/connection-changes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-private-endpoint.md
- [statement] AzureRM provider 3.93.0 historically rejected private_ip_address for a Static inbound endpoint with "Value for unconfigurable attribute". Issue #25026 records the reproducer and closure through #25035 on March 4, 2024; this is historical provider behavior, not evidence of a current Azure service restriction. (low confidence) — https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/25026 · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver
- [statement] Resolver endpoints require separate dedicated subnets delegated to Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers; the parent resolver references one VNet, and each endpoint belongs within that resolver's network. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets
- [statement] Azure DNS Private Resolver replaces self-managed DNS forwarding servers with managed inbound and outbound resolution between Azure and external private environments. Hybrid use still requires network connectivity, such as VPN or ExpressRoute. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://blog.brewedinthecloud.com/p/azure-dns-privateresolver/
- [statement] An inbound endpoint exposes a private IP that external DNS servers can use as a conditional-forwarding target. It resolves private zones linked to the endpoint VNet. An outbound endpoint supplies forwarding egress and has no equivalent client-facing listener IP. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/
- [statement] A forwarding rule targeting the resolver inbound endpoint must not be applied through a ruleset link to that inbound endpoint VNet: this can create a DNS forwarding loop. A wildcard rule also requires a target that can resolve public dependencies. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/
- [statement] For DNS troubleshooting, repeat one FQDN and record type from affected and control networks. Record the actual resolver, response code, answer, TTL and timing; test UDP and TCP separately before attributing timeouts to a loop. (medium confidence) — https://naxaya.com/articles/azure-dns-private-resolver-diagnose-forwarding-loop-before-changing-zones/ · keywords: Azure Private DNS Resolver · also: https://spmonkey.com/azure-dns-private-resolver-hybrid-dns-runbook/
